questions.solution:

In part (c) of the sentence, "with" is used, following the correlative conjunction "and" which is grammatically wrong.
Correlative conjunction both...and are always used in pair in a sentence.
For e.g.- She is both talented with hardworking.
She is both talented and hardworking.
Thus, the error 'with' will be rectified by 'and' to make the sentence contextually and grammatically correct.

Additional Information
Correlative conjunctions work in pairs to join words, phrases, or clauses; No sentence can be completed with any one of the pair.
List of Correlative conjunctions-
​Either---------------------or
Neither-------------------Nor
Not only------------------But also
No sooner----------------Than
Hardly/ Scarcely----------when, etc

Important Points

If ​a sentence starts with 'Hardly', 'Scarcely', 'No sooner', 'Not only', 'Neither' etc., the sentence formation following these conjunctions will be in inverted form i.e. helping verb + subject + main verb [here, 'Had + S + V3' or 'Did + S + V1'] but this does not make the sentence interrogative in meaning.
For e.g.- Hardly I saw him when I stopped my car.
Hardly did I see him when I stopped my car.

The Correct sentence- He was determined to both beat the record and win the crowd over.

questions.question: What can be reasonably inferred from the passage regarding the wetlands (beels) of Assam?

options.a: Their conservation and restoration would reduce the velocity and volume of floodwaters reaching human settlements during extreme rainfall.
options.b: Their transformation into agricultural land has successfully mitigated the hydraulic ferocity of flash floods in urban areas.
options.c: They were artificially engineered by disaster management authorities to act as longitudinal barriers against sediment deposition.
options.d: They are the primary source of the heavy silt that elevates the channel floor of the Brahmaputra River

questions.solution:
Solution
The correct answer is Option 1.

Key Points
Option 1: Their conservation and restoration would reduce the velocity and volume of floodwaters reaching human settlements during extreme rainfall.
This is correct. The passage explains that wetlands (beels) function as natural hydrological sinks by absorbing excess runoff during peak monsoon periods and releasing water gradually during dry periods. Therefore, restoring these wetlands would help reduce the intensity and speed of floodwaters reaching populated areas.
Option 2: Their transformation into agricultural land has successfully mitigated the hydraulic ferocity of flash floods in urban areas.
This is incorrect. The passage states the opposite: wetland encroachment for agriculture and urbanization has destroyed natural flood buffers, increasing unregulated runoff and worsening flood conditions.
Option 3: They were artificially engineered by disaster management authorities to act as longitudinal barriers against sediment deposition.
This is incorrect. The passage describes wetlands as natural ecological systems, not artificial structures. Longitudinal barriers refer to embankments, not wetlands.
Option 4: They are the primary source of the heavy silt that elevates the channel floor of the Brahmaputra River.
This is incorrect. The passage attributes sediment accumulation in the river channel to the restriction of lateral spill caused by embankments, not to wetlands.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1: Their conservation and restoration would reduce the velocity and volume of floodwaters reaching human settlements during extreme rainfall.

Additional Information
Wetlands (beels) act as natural flood-control systems by storing excess water and gradually releasing it, reducing sudden surges in river discharge.
The passage advocates wetland rejuvenation as part of a nature-based approach to flood management, replacing excessive dependence on artificial engineering solutions.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.
His strike rate in this series is 74.35, which is the higher than that of any other batsman.
questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is option 1) i.e. is the higher.

Explanation:

In the given sentence, ‘higher’ is a comparative degree.
The comparative degree is the form of an adverb or adjective modified by more or ending in -er that is used when comparing two things.
Generally, the definite article ‘the’ is not used with the comparative degree.
Thus, the use of the definite article 'the' is not needed and should be eliminated from the sentence.
Hence, the correct option is "is the higher".

We use 'the' in a comparative degree when we want to depict a parallel comparison. For example:
The more sugar you put in the dish, the sweeter it is.
The structure for using the in a comparative degree for the parallel comparison is :
The + comparative adjective + clause + the + comparative adjective + clause

Correct Sentence: His strike rate in this series is 74.35, which is higher than that of any other batsman.

questions.question:
Consider the following sentences:
(A) India must take its laws on waste seriously to stop microplastics pollution.
(B) India must take its laws on waste serious to stop microplastics pollution.
(C) India must take seriously its laws on waste to stop microplastics pollution.
(D) The laws must be took seriously to stop microplastics pollution.
Which of the above sentences is/are grammatically CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is 'Only (A)'.

Key Points
Sentence (A) is grammatically CORRECT.
The use of modal 'must' is correct. It is showing 'obligation'.
Adverb 'seriously' is qualifying the verb 'take' and the position of the adverb is also apt.
Sentence (B) is grammatically INCORRECT.
Adjective 'serious' should be replaced with adverb 'seriously' to qualify the verb 'take'.
​Sentence (C) is also INCORRECT.
'Take' is a transitive verb and it needs an object. The object here is 'its laws'.
We can't put an adverb between a verb and its direct object.
Thus, the position of 'seriously' is not correct.
​Sentence (D) is INCORRECT.
​The Sentence is in passive voice. We need V3 (taken), not V2 (took).
'must be took' should be replaced with 'must be taken'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 2).

Additional Information
Adjectives are the words that qualify a noun or a pronoun.
Ex: The movie was really good.
An adverb is a word that describes or gives more information about a verb, adjective, adverb, or phrase.
Ex: Walk carefully lest you should fall.
Ex: He is fast enough to be an athlete.

Passage: The precipitous melting of the polar ice caps has fundamentally transformed the Arctic from a peripheral, frozen wasteland into a central geopolitical (1) _________.
questions.solution:
Solution
The correct answer is 'Quagmire'.

Key Points
The passage describes a situation involving a "scramble to assert maritime claims" over trade routes and mineral wealth. This suggests a complex, difficult, and potentially trapped environment.
"Quagmire" (नाज़ुक स्थिति/दलदल) refers to a soft boggy area of land that yields underfoot, or metaphorically, an awkward, complex, or hazardous situation from which it is difficult to extricate oneself. This perfectly fits the "geopolitical scramble" mentioned.
"Sinecure" (आराम की नौकरी) is a position requiring little or no work but giving the holder status or financial benefit. This is logically irrelevant to a global resource scramble.
"Cynosure" (आकर्षण का केंद्र) refers to a person or thing that is the center of attention or admiration. While the Arctic is a center of attention, "quagmire" better captures the difficulty and conflict implied by the word "scramble."
"Paradigm" (प्रतिमान) is a typical example or pattern of something. While the Arctic is a new pattern of conflict, it is a neutral term that doesn't reflect the "high-stakes scramble" as accurately as "quagmire."
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.

As the "Great Thaw" accelerates, global powers are no longer merely observers of climate change but active participants in a high-stakes scramble to assert maritime claims over newly accessible trans-continental trade routes and vast, untapped mineral wealth. This environmental metamorphosis represents a profound strategic restructuring of international relations, where the once-impenetrable ice is replaced by overlapping zones of national interest. Given the extreme sensitivity of this frontier, it is essential that the Arctic Council (2) __________ a binding framework that prioritizes ecological preservation over short-term resource extraction.

However, the cooperative spirit of the past is under duress; not only (3) __________ the territorial disputes intensifying among the littoral states, but the increasing militarization of the Northern Sea Route also threatens the long-standing "Arctic Exceptionalism" that once kept the region insulated from global friction. The deployment of ice-class warships and the reopening of Cold War-era outposts signal a shift from scientific collaboration to securitized competition. Any attempt by a single nation to exploit the region’s sub-seabed resources without a robust, multilateral consensus will likely prove to be a (4) __________, leading to a cascade of irreversible environmental damage and a diplomatic fallout that would resonate far beyond the high latitudes.

Maritime Claims (समुद्री दावे): Assertions of sovereignty or control over specific areas of the ocean and the resources beneath them.

The base form of the verb is "formulate". This form remains constant regardless of whether the subject ("the Arctic Council") is singular or plural.
Option 1 ("should formulate") is a common auxiliary usage in British English, but in competitive exams like CAT/GMAT, the pure subjunctive "formulate" is considered more accurate and formal.
Option 3 ("is formulating") and Option 4 ("to formulate") are grammatically incorrect within the specific requirements of a subjunctive "that" clause.

The sentence begins with the negative/restrictive correlative conjunction "not only". In formal English, when a sentence or a clause starts with "not only", Grammatical Inversion must occur.
Inversion Rule: The auxiliary verb is placed before the subject. In this case, the subject is "the territorial disputes," which is a plural noun.
Since the subject is plural, the plural auxiliary verb "are" is required before the subject to maintain subject-verb agreement.
Option 2 ("is actually") is singular and fails the agreement test with "disputes".

pause - A temporary break or cessation in activity; a momentary stop or hesitation. In the sentence, it suggests that the library in the palace is so impressive that it would make anyone pause or momentarily stop to appreciate its beauty.

imitation - The act of replicating or mimicking something, often with the intention of resembling or copying the original. Here, it refers to the fact that the high roof in the palace is designed to resemble or imitate the one found in Windsor Castle.

Read the passage and answer the following question:

In the contemporary administrative framework of India, the roles of Divisional Commissioner and District Collector constitute significant pillars of regional governance, though they differ considerably in jurisdiction, authority, and functional responsibilities. While both positions are occupied by senior civil servants, their administrative scope and operational focus vary according to the level at which they function within the governmental hierarchy.

The District Collector, often referred to as the District Magistrate or Deputy Commissioner in certain states, serves as the chief executive authority at the district level. Since the district represents the fundamental unit of administration, the Collector is entrusted with responsibilities such as revenue administration, maintenance of law and order, implementation of developmental schemes, disaster management, and coordination of electoral processes. Owing to constant interaction with local institutions and the public, the office of the Collector remains closely associated with grassroots governance and immediate administrative concerns.

In contrast, the Divisional Commissioner operates at a broader regional level and supervises the administration of multiple districts grouped within a division. Rather than directly addressing routine district-level issues, the Commissioner primarily undertakes inspection, coordination, policy monitoring, and administrative review. The office ensures consistency in governance, evaluates the performance of district administrations, and facilitates communication between the state government and subordinate administrative units. This supervisory role enables the Commissioner to maintain administrative uniformity across an entire division.

Furthermore, the distinction between the two offices may be understood through the nature of their decision-making responsibilities. The Collector functions as an executive authority directly involved in field administration and public service delivery, whereas the Divisional Commissioner acts as a supervisory and appellate authority overseeing the functioning of several Collectors simultaneously. Consequently, while the Collector focuses on operational administration within a single district, the Commissioner concentrates on broader regional coordination and institutional efficiency.

In essence, the relationship between the Divisional Commissioner and the District Collector reflects a structured administrative hierarchy designed to balance local governance with regional supervision. Together, these offices contribute to effective policy implementation, administrative accountability, and coordinated governance across the state system.

questions.question: I remember them taking me to the Zoo.

options.a: I remember having being taken to the Zoo.
options.b: I remember to be taken to the Zoo.
options.c: I remember being taken to the Zoo.
options.d: I remember I was taken to the Zoo.

questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is "I remember being taken to  the Zoo."

Key Points
The original sentence is: "I remember them taking me to the Zoo," which is in the active voice.
The structure for active voice sentence is: Subject + verb + object + gerund(verb+ing) + object
Here, in the given sentence:
"I" is the subject.
"Remember" is the verb.
"Them" is the object.
"Taking" is the gerund (verb+ing).
"Me to the Zoo" is another object.
To convert this sentence into passive voice, we switch the positions of the subject and object, and adjust the form of the verb accordingly.
The gerund "taking" becomes "being taken" in passive voice.
The structure for the passive voice sentence is: Subject + verb + being + past participle + object+ preposition+ object
Reviewing the alternatives, we find:
"I remember having being taken to the Zoo." - This sentence is grammatically incorrect because it combines "having" and "being," which don't go together.
"I remember to be taken to the Zoo." - This does not correctly maintain the original meaning because "I remember to be" is used to express a future responsibility, not a past event.
"I remember being taken to the Zoo." - This choice correctly maintains the original meaning and tense while using the correct passive voice.
"I remember I was taken to the Zoo." - This sentence is also correct, but it is less smooth and less commonly used compared to option 3.
Therefore, "I remember being taken to the Zoo," is the correct conversion of the given sentence into the passive voice, maintaining the original meaning and tense.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

Directions: In this section, the item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and the sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labeled as P, Q, R, and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly.
S1 : Environmental campaigns are marked by rousing calls for collective, transformative action on a global scale.
S6 : For example, a farmer producer organization in Anantapur needs to know what changes to make to improve income and adapt to a water-stressed future, or a conservation group in Wayanad needs a list of native species for landscape restoration work.
P : Addressing this bedrock issue of data access is vitally important at a time when the impacts of climate change are manifesting with increasing severity.
Q : For human settlements to thrive in a climate-changing world, planning must be informed by a deep understanding of local ecologies and socio-economic contexts.
R : But to achieve this, access to the right data is essential.
S : It has pushed us into new territory where the contextual and traditional knowledge of farmers and indigenous communities needs to be integrated with better data.
The correct sequence should be:

Solution

The correct answer is 'QRPS.'

While arranging the parts of the sentence given in the options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them, so let's find out.

statement in the sequence should be the one that best connects with S1.

R follows Q because in Q to for achieving thrive in the climate-changing world we need access to the right data given.
P follows R because it further extends the information regarding access to the data.
S is directly connected with S6 because addressing the access to the right data in P which will push us into new territory is given in S and it is elaborated in S6 with an example.
​​​Therefore, the correct sequence is 'S1QRPSS6'.

Correct Sentence
S1 : Environmental campaigns are marked by rousing calls for collective, transformative action on a global scale.
Q  : For human settlements to thrive in a climate-changing world, planning must be informed by a deep understanding of local ecologies and socio-economic contexts.
R  : But to achieve this, access to the right data is essential.

S  : It has pushed us into new territory where the contextual and traditional knowledge of farmers and indigenous communities needs to be integrated with better data.
S6 : For example, a farmer producer organization in Anantapur needs to know what changes to make to improve income and adapt to a water-stressed future, or a conservation group in Wayanad needs a list of native species for landscape restoration work.

Context from passage: "...the realization that its economic destiny is inextricably tethered to the stability of the 'global commons' necessitates that the Ministry of Defence (2) __________ a more expansive naval posture."
questions.solution:
Solution
The correct answer is 'adopt'.

Key Points
The sentence contains the verb "necessitates that," which is a classic trigger for the mandative subjunctive mood in formal, academic English.
When verbs of requirement, demand, or necessity (such as necessitate, demand, insist, require, suggest) are followed by a "that" clause, the verb in that clause must be in its base form (the infinitive without "to").
The base form of the verb is "adopt." In the subjunctive mood, this form does not change to "adopts" even though the subject ("the Ministry of Defence") is singular.
Option 2 ("adopts") is the indicative form, which is used for factual statements but is grammatically incorrect in a subjunctive "that" clause.
Option 3 ("to adopt") and Option 4 ("is adopting") do not satisfy the structural requirements for a finite verb in this subjunctive construction.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.
Complete Passage: The geopolitical calculus of the 21st century has undergone a fundamental (1) Metamorphosis, shifting the center of gravity from the continental heartlands of Eurasia to the vast maritime expanses of the Indo-Pacific. For a nation like India, which has historically been preoccupied with the "tectonic" frictions of its land borders and the constant vigilance required by its neighbors, the realization that its economic destiny is inextricably tethered to the stability of the "global commons" necessitates that the Ministry of Defence (2) adopt a more expansive naval posture. A "Blue Water" navy is not merely a collection of sophisticated hulls and high-decibel rhetoric, but a projection of national will across the high seas; however, the transition from a brown-water force is fraught with the (3) __________ of balancing capital-intensive carrier groups against the immediate, often mundane, requirements of coastal security and disaster relief. This strategic pivot requires a recalibration of budgetary priorities, often sparking intense inter-service debates over the allocation of dwindling resources. Such a transition is further complicated by the need to integrate emerging technologies like unmanned autonomous vehicles into a traditional command structure that has long prioritized manned platforms.

Furthermore, scarcely (4) __________ the strategic community reached a fragile consensus on the necessity of a three-carrier fleet to ensure continuous carrier availability on both seaboards when the rapid proliferation of "Anti-Access/Area Denial" (A2/AD) capabilities by regional rivals forced a radical reassessment of such carrier-centric doctrines. Should India (5) __________ to ignore the imperative of underwater domain awareness and the modernization of its aging submarine fleet, the resulting vulnerability in the "silent service" could prove to be a cataclysm for its energy security and regional status. The margin for error in these high-stakes maritime maneuvers is razor-thin, as any perceived weakness could embolden adversaries to challenge established maritime boundaries. Ultimately, the quest for naval dominance must evolve into a robust mechanism for maintaining regional stability, moving beyond the trap of reactive posturing toward a proactive, deterrent-based framework.

Additional Information
Tethered (बंधा हुआ): Tied or restricted with a rope or chain; in this context, it means India's economic success is "tied" to the safety of the oceans.
Inextricably (अविभाज्य रूप से): In a way that is impossible to disentangle or separate.
Naval Posture: The general disposition, attitude, or strategic position of a navy in response to a given situation.

Option 2 ("was") is considered informal and is typically penalized in high-stakes competitive exams like CAT/GMAT when used in hypothetical conditionals.
Option 3 ("had") would require a past participle (e.g., Should India had ignored), but it doesn't fit the "to ignore" infinitive structure. Option 4 ("is") is the indicative present and cannot be used in a hypothetical "should" inversion.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.

questions.question:
The following passage consists of six sentences. The first and the sixth sentences are given. The middle four sentences in each have been removed and jumbled up. These are labelled P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.
S1: The empowerment of women and the improvement of their political, social, economic and health status is a highly important end in itself.
P: In addition, it is essential for the achievement of sustainable development.
Q: In all parts of the world, women are facing threats to their lives, health and well-being as a result of being overburdened with work and of their lack of power and influence.
R: In most regions of the world, women receive less formal education than men, and at the same time, women's own knowledge, abilities and coping mechanisms often go unrecognized.
S: The full participation and partnership of both women and men is required in productive and reproductive life, including shared responsibilities for the care and nurturing of children and maintenance of the household.
S6: The power relations that impede women's attainment of healthy and fulfilling lives operate at many levels of society, from the most personal to the highly public.
questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is 'PSQR.'

Key Points
While arranging the parts of the passage given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them, so let’s find out.
The first
statement in the sequence should be the one that best connects with S1.
It should be a continuation or extension of S1.
P follows S1 because it is adding more information to the empowerment of women.
S follows P because it is talking about requirement of full participation and partnership of both women and men.
Q follows S because it is talking about the lack of power and influence.
R is directly connected to S6.
S6 provides a conclusion to the story.
Therefore, the sequence is 'S1PSQRS6.'
Thus, the correct answer is 'PSQR.'
​​The correct sequence:
​

S1- The empowerment of women and the improvement of their political, social, economic and health status is a highly important end in itself.

P- In addition, it is essential for the achievement of sustainable development.

S- The full participation and partnership of both women and men is required in productive and reproductive life, including shared responsibilities for the care and nurturing of children and maintenance of the household.

Q- In all parts of the world, women are facing threats to their lives, health and well-being as a result of being overburdened with work and of their lack of power and influence.

R- In most regions of the world, women receive less formal education than men, and at the same time, women's own knowledge, abilities and coping mechanisms often go unrecognized.

Clues include pronouns, like he, she, it, this, that, these, those; adverbs like formally, really; article a, an and the; definers like actually, finally, another; connectors like but, yet, both, also and neither nor, or, however, nevertheless.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The soldiers, besides the general, has taken up arms against the king.
questions.solution:
The error lies in option (b).

If two subjects are separated by 'besides', the verb agrees with the main subject.

For example: The thief, besides his apprentice, has been caught by the police.

Similarly, in this context, 'soldiers' is the main subject. As the subject is plural in form, the verb that must agree with it must also be plural.

Hence, 'has' must be replaced by 'have'.

Thus, the error is in option (b) the general has taken.

Therefore, the corrected form of the sentence is: The soldiers, besides the general, have taken up arms against the king.

Additional Information:
If two subjects are separated by anything except "and", the verb agrees with the main subject. The list of such words is:

As well as
Like
Unlike
Besides
In addition to
With
Together with
Along with
Including

questions.question: A, B and C can reap a field in 2 days; B, C and D in 3 days; C, D and A in 7 days; D, A and B in 10 days. In what time can A, B, C and D together reap it?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let Total Work = LCM(2, 3, 7, 10) = 210 units.
Sum of 1-day work (efficiencies) of all 4 groups = (210 ÷ 2) + (210 ÷ 3) + (210 ÷ 7) + (210 ÷ 10) = 105 + 70 + 30 + 21 = 226.

Since each person is included in exactly 3 groups, their combined actual efficiency = 226 / 3 units/day.

Time required = Total Work ÷ Actual Efficiency = 210 ÷ (226 / 3) = 630 / 226 days.
∴ The correct answer is 630/226 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by (A + B + C) = 2 days
Time taken by (B + C + D) = 3 days
Time taken by (C + D + A) = 7 days
Time taken by (D + A + B) = 10 days

Formula Used:
Total Work = LCM of time taken
Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time
Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

Person	Days	Total Work	Efficiency
A + B + C	2	210	105
B + C + D	3	70
C + D + A	7	30
D + A + B	10	21

⇒ Sum of the efficiencies = 105 + 70 + 30 + 21 = 226 units/day
⇒ (A + B + C) + (B + C + D) + (C + D + A) + (D + A + B) = 226
⇒ 3A + 3B + 3C + 3D = 226
⇒ 3 × (A + B + C + D) = 226
⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + B + C + D) = 226 / 3 units/day
⇒ Time required = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency
⇒ Time required = 210 ÷ (226 / 3)
⇒ Time required = (210 × 3) / 226 = 630 / 226 days
∴ The correct answer is 630/226 days.

Additional Information
Time and Work LCM Method

Always assume Total Work as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the given days to make calculations fraction-free. Efficiency is calculated as Total Work ÷ Time.

Combined Group Work Principle

When individuals work in overlapping pairs or triplets, sum their combined group efficiencies and divide by the frequency of each person's appearance to find the actual joint efficiency.

Work and Time Relationship

Time and efficiency are inversely proportional. A higher combined efficiency directly results in proportionally less time taken to complete the assigned task.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

P. due to the lofty hilly terrain, curves and cliffs
Q. the route to Badrinath
R. is one of the most arduous ones
S. amidst the most scenically beautiful place on the earth
questions.solution:
The correct answer is QSRP.

Part Q sets the context by specifying the subject of the sentence ('the route to Badrinath').

Part S adds context about the location ('amidst the most scenically beautiful place on the earth').

Part R provides information about the nature of the route ('is one of the most arduous ones').

Part P explains the reason for the arduous nature ('due to the lofty hilly terrain, curves, and cliffs').

Thus, the complete meaningful sentence reads: 'The route to Badrinath amidst the most scenically beautiful place on the earth is one of the most arduous ones due to the lofty hilly terrain, curves, and cliffs.'

questions.question:
Comprehension:(Que No. 21 - 25) Reading Comprehension Passage (420 Words)

The trajectory of Indian cinema underwent a profound ontological shift in 1955 with the release of Satyajit Ray’s directorial debut, Pather Panchali. Rejecting the melodramatic escapism and rigid theatricality that then dominated the commercial mainstream, Ray embraced a poignant aesthetic of poetic realism deeply influenced by Italian neorealism and classical Bengali literature. Through the immortal Apu Trilogy-comprising Pather Panchali, Aparajito, and Apur Sansar-he articulated a universal humanism that transcended socio-geographical boundaries. His cinematic architecture was not reliant on artificial narrative contrivances; instead, it drew its breathtaking verisimilitude from the quiet indignities of poverty, the resilience of the human spirit, and the subtle, rhythmic cadence of everyday rural existence. Beyond his mastery of the lens, Ray was a quintessential Renaissance man whose polymathic genius extended far beyond directing. As a fiercely independent auteur, he frequently maintained total creative autonomy by scripting his own narratives, designing intricate storyboards, composing original musical scores, and illustrating promotional publicity material. His thematic canvas was remarkably expansive, seamlessly traversing historical tragedies like Shatranj Ke Khiladi, incisive critiques of urban bourgeois morality in Mahanagar and Charulata, and captivating children’s literature featuring iconic detectives like Feluda. Across these disparate genres, Ray’s directorial gaze remained anchored in a profound empathy for his characters, dissecting complex socio-political dynamics-such as the erosion of feudal hierarchies and the evolving role of women in modern India-without ever devolving into didactic moralizing. The global culmination of this illustrious career occurred in 1992 when the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences conferred upon him an Honorary Oscar for Lifetime Achievement. Bedridden and gravely ill in a Calcutta hospital, Ray received the statuette via a live satellite feed during the 64th Academy Awards ceremony, describing it as the 'best achievement' of his cinematic journey. This accolade was not merely a retrospective validation by the Western film establishment; it was a testament to his uncompromising artistic integrity. Prior to this coronation, he had already garnered the Golden Lion at Venice and the Golden Bear at Berlin, alongside France's highest civilian honor, the Legion of Honour, cementing his stature alongside titans like Kurosawa, Bergman, and Fellini. Ultimately, Satyajit Ray’s monumental achievement lies in his ability to decolonize the cinematic apparatus, utilizing a quintessentially Western technological medium to articulate an authentically Indian vernacular. His oeuvre remains an enduring masterclass in visual storytelling, demonstrating that profound universality is most effectively achieved not through generic homogenization, but through an uncompromising, deeply compassionate immersion into the hyper-local specifics of human life.

Question:
What is the primary focus of the passage?

options.a: A technical analysis of Ray's camera equipment and lighting methodologies in comparison to Italian neorealist directors.
options.b: An exploration of Satyajit Ray’s polymathic cinematic genius, thematic depth, and global recognition culminating in his Lifetime Achievement Oscar.
options.c: A critique of the Western Academy Awards for delaying the recognition of Eastern filmmakers until the very end of their careers.
options.d: A biographical comparison between Satyajit Ray's detective fiction and his historical dramas like Shatranj Ke Khiladi.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option B.

Key Points: Option A is incorrect because although the passage mentions Ray's influence from Italian neorealism, it does not discuss his camera equipment, lighting techniques, or technical comparisons with other directors.

Option B is correct because the passage primarily focuses on Satyajit Ray's revolutionary contribution to Indian cinema, his poetic realism, creative versatility, exploration of social themes, and international recognition, including his Honorary Oscar for Lifetime Achievement.

Option C is incorrect because the passage does not criticize the Academy Awards or suggest bias against Eastern filmmakers. Instead, it presents Ray's Oscar as a significant recognition of his artistic legacy.

Option D is incorrect because the passage mentions Ray's work in different genres, including detective fiction and historical dramas, only to demonstrate his creative range. It does not provide a comparison between these works.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

questions.question:

"The architect could have been designing the building."

options.b: The building could have been designed.

Final sentence: The building could have been being designed.

Options 1 and 2 lose the continuous aspect, and option 3 loses the perfect aspect.

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

Take a pair of binoculars with you lest you all should miss the chance of looking at the distant scenes.

options.a: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes would missed by you all.
options.b: Let a pair of binoculars taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.
options.c: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you otherwise the chance of looking at the distant scenes would be missed by you all.
options.d: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.

questions.solution:
Rule: An imperative becomes Let + object + be + past participle; the “lest ... should” clause also turns passive: lest + new subject + should be + past participle.
Explicit changes: - “Take a pair of binoculars with you” → “Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you”. - “you all should miss the chance” → “the chance ... should be missed by you all”. - Keep “lest”; it is followed by “should”.
Final sentence: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.

Option 1 has “would missed”, option 2 omits “be”, and option 3 replaces “lest ... should” with “otherwise - would”.
questions.conceptTested: An imperative sentence becomes 'Let + object + be + past participle', and the 'lest ... should' clause transforms to 'lest + new subject + should be + past participle'.

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

options.a: The professor said, "I've never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any of my classes."
options.b: The professor admitted, "I'd never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any class."
options.c: The professor admitted, "I have not deliver a lecture on that particular topic in any of my classes."
options.d: The professor said, "I have never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in none of my classes."

questions.solution:
Rule: While converting to direct speech, use “said”, restore first - person pronouns, move the past perfect forward to the present perfect and change “that” to “this”.
Explicit changes: - “admitted that he had never delivered” becomes said, “I've never delivered”. - “that particular topic” becomes “this particular topic”. - “his classes” becomes “my classes”.
Final sentence: The professor said, \"I've never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any of my classes.\"

Option 2 keeps the past perfect, option 3 has “have not deliver”, and option 4 has a double negative (“never ... none”).

questions.solution:

The students → object the students

to clean → clean ('to' is dropped after 'make' in the active)

was spoken → spoke

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

He said that he would not tolerate such nuisance in the office.

options.a: That such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated had been said by him.
options.b: It was said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.
options.c: It had been said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.
options.d: That such nuisance in the office would not be tolerating had been said by him.

questions.solution:
Rule: For "said that ...", the passive uses It was said by + agent + that - clause; the verb inside the clause also becomes passive: would tolerate $\rightarrow$ would be tolerated.
Explicit changes: He said $\rightarrow$ It was said by him

he would not tolerate such nuisance $\rightarrow$ such nuisance would not be tolerated

Final sentence: It was said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.

Options 1 and 3 use "had been said" (wrong tense), and option 4 uses "would not be tolerating".

questions.question:

Final sentence: The husband was advised by the wife to maintain silence when yoga was being practised by her.

Option 1 uses "was practised" (wrong tense); options 3 and 4 misplace the agents.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 9
questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question:

Something has gone wrong with the flow of information. It's not just that different people are drawing subtly different conclusions from the same evidence. It seems like different intellectual communities no longer share basic foundational beliefs. Maybe nobody cares about the truth anymore, as some have started to worry. Maybe political allegiance has replaced basic reasoning skills. Maybe we've all become trapped in echo chambers of our own making - wrapping ourselves in an intellectually impenetrable layer of likeminded friends and web pages and social media feeds. But there are two very different phenomena at play here, each of which subvert the flow of information in very distinct ways. Let's call them echo chambers and epistemic bubbles. Both are social structures that systematically exclude sources of information. Both exaggerate their members' confidence in their beliefs. But they work in entirely different ways, and they require very different modes of intervention. An epistemic bubble is when you don't hear people from the other side. An echo chamber is what happens when you don't trust people from the other side. Current usage has blurred this crucial distinction, so let me introduce a somewhat artificial taxonomy. An 'epistemic bubble' is an informational network from which relevant voices have been excluded by omission. That omission might be purposeful: we might be selectively avoiding contact with contrary views because, say, they make us uncomfortable. As social scientists tell us, we like to engage in selective exposure, seeking out information that confirms our own worldview. But that omission can also be entirely inadvertent. Even if we're not actively trying to avoid disagreement, our Facebook friends tend to share our views and interests. When we take networks built for social reasons and start using them as our information feeds, we tend to miss out on contrary views and run into exaggerated degrees of agreement. An 'echo chamber' is a social structure from which other relevant voices have been actively discredited. Where an epistemic bubble merely omits contrary views, an echo chamber brings its members to actively distrust outsiders. In their book Echo Chamber: Rush Limbaugh and the Conservative Media Establishment (2010), Kathleen Hall Jamieson and Frank Cappella offer a groundbreaking analysis of the phenomenon. For them, an echo chamber is something like a cult. A cult isolates its members by actively alienating them from any outside sources. Those outsides are actively labelled as malignant and untrustworthy. A cult member's trust is narrowed, aimed with laser-like focus on certain insider voices. In epistemic bubbles, other voices are not heard; in echo chambers, other voices are actively undermined. The way to break an echo chamber is not to wave "the facts" in the faces of its members. It is to attack the echo chamber at its root and repair that broken trust.

Question: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.a: The breakdown in the flow of information can be understood by distinguishing between echo chambers and epistemic bubbles, which operate differently and require different solutions.
options.b: Echo chambers and epistemic bubbles are the same phenomenon.
options.c: People no longer care about truth at all.
options.d: Social media is the only cause of misinformation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option A.

Key Points
The passage explains the differences between echo chambers and epistemic bubbles, outlining how echo chambers actively discredit outside voices while epistemic bubbles simply omit them. It emphasizes that understanding these differences is crucial because they require very different modes of intervention.

options.b: of tourists every year who are

questions.solution:
The error is in part C: fascinating by should be fascinated by.

questions.question:
The sentence below has errors in two parts which are highlighted in bold. Identify the same.

The reef is on risk of (A) losing its coveted World Heritage Status on occasion of (B) ocean warming, fuelled by (C) climate change, which is damaging its health(D).
questions.solution:
The errors are in parts A and B.

A: "on risk of" $\rightarrow$ at risk of (fixed phrase meaning "in danger of").
B: "on occasion of" $\rightarrow$ on account of / because of; a cause is needed here, while "on the occasion of" means "at the time of an event".
Correct sentence: The reef is at risk of losing its coveted World Heritage Status on account of ocean warming, fuelled by climate change, which is damaging its health.

Parts C and D are correct, so the answer is BA.

questions.question:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.

questions.solution:
The error lies in part 3: will be coming.
Rule & Explanation: The future continuous tense ('will be coming') expresses an action in progress at a specific time in the future. However, receiving news and experiencing emotional shock occurs as a punctual event, not a continuous process. When stating the predictable effect of dramatic news, English uses the simple future: 'will come as a terrible shock' (or 'came as a terrible shock').
Correct sentence: The news that the plane had crashed will come as a terrible shock.

questions.question:
Change the following passive voice sentence into active voice by selecting the correct option.

The Railways Ministry has been upgrading railway stations across India over the last decade.

options.a: Railway stations across India have been being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.
options.b: Railway stations have been upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.
options.c: Railway stations across India have been upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.
options.d: Railway stations across India are being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.

questions.solution:
Note: The given sentence is in the active voice (the doer, the Railways Ministry, is the subject), so it has to be changed into the passive voice.
Important Note: The SSC answer key marks Option C as correct. However, from the perspective of standard tense conversion, Option A is the grammatically precise passive form of the given Present Perfect Continuous sentence. SSC has accepted Option C, which uses the Present Perfect Passive form, as the official answer.

Rule

Present perfect continuous active (has/have been + V - ing) → has/have been being + V³ in the passive.

Explicit changes

Object "railway stations across India" → subject (plural → have)

has been upgrading → have been being upgraded

The Railways Ministry → by the Railways Ministry

over the last decade → no change

Final sentence

Railway stations across India have been being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade. (Option A)

Why Option C was accepted by SSC: Option C uses the Present Perfect Passive structure (have been upgraded) instead of the exact Present Perfect Continuous Passive structure (have been being upgraded). The continuous passive form is grammatically possible but is uncommon and considered awkward in normal usage. Therefore, SSC has marked Option C as the official answer, while Option A is the structurally precise tense conversion.

tags.conceptTested: Conversion of a Present Perfect Continuous passive sentence to active voice.

questions.question:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.

They have been constructing the new metro line in Pune for two years.

options.a: The new metro line in Pune is constructed for two years.
options.b: The new metro line in Pune has been constructed for two years.
options.c: The new metro line in Pune has been being constructed for two years.
options.d: The new metro line in Pune will be constructed for two years.

Present perfect continuous active (have/has been + V - ing) → has/have been being + V³ in the passive.

Explicit changes

Object "the new metro line in Pune" → subject (singular → has)

have been constructing → has been being constructed

They → dropped (a vague doer is usually omitted)

for two years → no change

Final sentence

The new metro line in Pune has been being constructed for two years.

Options A, B and D change the tense (simple present, present perfect and simple future).

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The project is rumored to be finished ahead of schedule.

options.a: Someone is rumored to finish the project ahead of schedule.
options.b: They are rumored that the project will be finished ahead of schedule.
options.c: People say that the project will be finished ahead of schedule.

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

Has she left the apartment?

options.a: Is the apartment left by her?
options.b: Had the apartment been left by her?
options.c: Has the apartment been left by her?
options.d: Have the apartment been left by her?

Rule

Present perfect question "Has + subject + V³ + object?" → Has/Have + object + been + V³ + by + subject?

Explicit changes

the apartment → subject (singular → has)

Has ... left → Has ... been left

she → by her

Has the apartment been left by her?

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The teacher gave the students a difficult assignment.

options.a: A difficult assignment were given the students by the teacher.
options.b: The students were given a difficult assignment by the teacher.
options.c: The students were giving a difficult assignment by the teacher.
options.d: A difficult assignment was given to the students by the teacher.

questions.solution:
Rule

"Give" has two objects. In the passive, the indirect object (the person) usually becomes the subject; simple past → was/were + V³.

Explicit changes

the students → subject (plural → were)

gave → were given

a difficult assignment → retained object

The teacher → by the teacher

Final sentence

The students were given a difficult assignment by the teacher.

Option D (direct object as subject) is also grammatically possible, but the standard passive of such sentences makes the person the subject, as in option B. Option A has "assignment were" and option C ("were giving") is not passive.

questions.question:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.

They have announced that the school will reopen after Pongal holidays.

options.a: It was announced that the school will reopen after Pongal holidays.
options.b: That the school will reopen was announced by them after Pongal holidays.
options.c: It has been announced that the school will reopen after Pongal holidays.
options.d: The school has announced that it will reopen after Pongal holidays.

questions.solution:
Rule

In sentences where an active subject introduces a statement with a reporting verb followed by a that - clause (Subject + have + V³ + that - clause), the standard impersonal passive construction uses: 'It + has been + V³ + that - clause'.

Explicit changes

• The dummy pronoun 'It' is introduced as the grammatical subject.
• Present perfect active 'have announced' transforms to present perfect passive 'has been announced' (agreeing with singular 'It').
• The that - clause remains intact.

Final sentence

It has been announced that the school will reopen after Pongal holidays.

Option 1 incorrectly shifts the tense to simple past ('was announced').
questions.conceptTested: Impersonal passive constructions with reporting verbs and that-clauses use 'It + has been + V3 + that-clause' in present perfect.

tags.conceptTested: Impersonal passive constructions with reporting verbs and that-clauses use 'It + has been + V3 + that-clause' in present perfect.

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

They used 1,45,000 eggs to make the largest omelette in the world.

options.a: The 1,45,000 eggs were used to make the largest omelette in the world.
options.b: 1,45,000 eggs were used to make the largest omelette in the world.
options.c: 1,45,000 eggs had been used to make the largest omelette in the world.
options.d: 1,45,000 eggs were used to be made the largest omelette in the world.

questions.solution:
Rule

Simple past active (Subject + V² + Object) transforms to passive: Object + were + V³ ('were used').

Explicit changes

• Object '1, 45, 000 eggs' becomes the subject.
• Simple past verb 'used' transforms to 'were used' (agreeing with plural 'eggs').
• The infinitive purpose clause 'to make the largest omelette in the world' remains active and unamended.

Final sentence

1, 45, 000 eggs were used to make the largest omelette in the world.

Option 1 inserts an uncalled - for definite article 'The', Option 3 incorrectly alters tense to past perfect ('had been used'), and Option 4 creates an ungrammatical infinitive ('used to be made').

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.

It is believed that the suspect has fled the country.

options.a: The suspect believed to have fled the country.
options.b: They believe the suspect has fled the country.
options.c: It believes the suspect has fled the country.
options.d: Believing the suspect has fled the country.

questions.solution:
Rule

The impersonal passive construction 'It is believed that...' converts into active voice by supplying an active plural indefinite subject such as 'They' or 'People', followed by the simple present verb 'believe'.

Explicit changes

• Supply general active subject 'They'.
• Passive 'is believed' transforms into active simple present 'believe'.
• The subordinate clause 'the suspect has fled the country' follows directly.

Final sentence

questions.question:

questions.solution:
Rule: Causative Verbs in Active vs. Passive
• When the causative verb make is used in the passive voice, it takes a full to - infinitive: 'was made to apologize'.

• Agent 'his mother' becomes the active subject 'The mother'.
• Passive 'was made to apologize' becomes active 'made the child apologize'.

Rule: Correlative Conjunction - “Not only ... but also”

The error lies in Part (2). The sentence uses the incorrect structure “does not only reflect ... but also undermines”. When “not only ... but also” is used to connect two parallel predicates, the correct construction is “not only reflects ... but also undermines.”

Correct: That certain state governments have invoked archaic laws to suppress dissent not only reflects legal opportunism but also undermines the constitutional ethos.

What does Advaita primarily teach?

Advaita, rooted in Adi Shankaracharya’s teachings, emphasizes that the Atman (individual self) and Brahman (universal consciousness) are one. It rejects dualism and ego - driven separation, instead promoting unity, empathy, and harmony among all beings and the natural world.
